title: Bio/chem uplift
summary: Studies in early 2024 found little or no uplift for biological attack planning. By 2025–26 models beat PhD experts on knowledge and troubleshooting tests, and labs began treating their models as capable of meaningful uplift.
definition: Bio/chem uplift is the extent to which AI models could help people cause harm with biological or chemical weapons beyond what they could do with the internet alone.
development: In January 2024, red-team studies from RAND and OpenAI found no significant or only mild uplift. Since then, models have overtaken experts on virology troubleshooting and on UK AISI's biology questions, and Anthropic (May 2025) and OpenAI (July 2025) applied their highest deployed bio safeguards as a precaution. In October 2025 a Science paper showed that AI protein-design tools could slip past DNA-synthesis screening until patched, and by June 2026 Anthropic called its judgement that Mythos 5 stays below the next threshold much less clear-cut than for earlier models.
methods: It is measured with knowledge and troubleshooting benchmarks, uplift trials with human participants, and labs' own threshold decisions. Benchmark scores do not show whether someone could actually carry out an attack, and threshold decisions are the labs' own judgements; this page describes findings only at the level of the sources' summaries.

chart.title: UK AISI Biology QA: best model's score relative to PhD-holder experts
chart.yLabel: Score relative to PhD experts (1.0 = expert baseline)
chart.caveat: Approximate: values digitised from AISI's Figure 5 (±0.03), x = model release month, models anonymised. PhD holders score about 38% in absolute terms. Filled points match the report text (models first reached the expert baseline in 2024 and now exceed it by up to 60%).

entries.title: The Operational Risks of AI in Large-Scale Biological Attacks: Results of a Red-Team Study
entries.quote: no statistically significant difference in the viability of plans generated with or without LLM assistance
entries.note: The baseline: with 2023-era models, red teams planning a biological attack did no better than with the internet alone.

entries.title: Building an early warning system for LLM-aided biological threat creation
entries.quote: we found that GPT‑4 provides at most a mild uplift in biological threat creation accuracy
entries.note: Uplift study with experts and students; the small gains were not statistically significant.

entries.title: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT): A Multimodal Virology Q&A Benchmark
entries.org: SecureBio, Center for AI Safety et al.
entries.quote: the most performant LLM, OpenAI's o3, reaches 43.8% accuracy
entries.note: On expert-written lab troubleshooting questions, o3 outperformed 94% of virologists, who averaged 22.1% within their own sub-areas.

entries.title: Activating AI Safety Level 3 protections
entries.quote: We are deploying Claude Opus 4 with our ASL-3 measures as a precautionary and provisional action.
entries.note: The first time a lab deployed a model under bio-focused ASL-3 safeguards, because it could no longer rule out the threshold.

entries.title: ChatGPT agent System Card
entries.quote: We have decided to treat this launch as High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain
entries.note: OpenAI's first launch treated as High bio/chem capability under its Preparedness Framework, also as a precaution.

entries.title: Strengthening nucleic acid biosecurity screening against generative protein design tools
entries.org: Wittmann et al. (Microsoft and partners), Science
entries.quote: identifying a vulnerability where AI-redesigned sequences could not be detected reliably by current tools
entries.note: AI protein-design tools could produce variants that DNA synthesis screening missed. Patches were developed and deployed with synthesis providers before publication.

entries.title: Frontier AI Trends Report
entries.quote: Models now outperform PhD-level experts on open-ended questions, protocol generation, and lab-based troubleshooting.
entries.note: Non-experts using frontier models had 4.7× higher odds of writing a feasible viral-recovery protocol than those using only the internet.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Mythos Preview (biological risk)
entries.quote: a view of the model as a powerful force-multiplier of existing capabilities
entries.note: Red teamers found strong synthesis of published knowledge but weak novel planning. Anthropic judged it below the novel-weapons (CB-2) threshold.

entries.title: System Card: Claude Fable 5 & Claude Mythos 5
entries.quote: this is a much less clear judgment than for previous models
entries.note: Anthropic treats Mythos 5 as CB-1 capable. It judges it still below CB-2 but says it can likely accelerate well-resourced expert teams.
